How is acute chest syndrome defined?
A new infiltrate on the chest X-ray with fever, chest pain, cough or hypoxia.
How is acute chest syndrome treated?

How is a stroke treated in sickle cell disease?

What are the features of splenic sequestration?
Sudden pallor, an enlarging spleen, a fall in haemoglobin of 2 g/dL or more, and shock.
What volume of blood is transfused in splenic sequestration?

How is an aplastic crisis told apart from a haemolytic crisis?
An aplastic crisis has low reticulocytes and no increase in jaundice; a haemolytic crisis has high reticulocytes and deeper jaundice.
